title: Friends who let him down and why he left show business for a while
summary: A friend never came to take him to a parade gig; both men trade stories of disappointment, and he left public life until well.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Uh-huh.

'Well, I promised so and so I'd bring him down to so and so and so, and here he comes in and starts out with me, 'Well, you're going somewhere with me.' Well, I don't feel good. 'You know,' what do you mean you don't feel good? You're supposed to be feeling good. 'I'm supposed to be feeling good.' Ain't that cool?
Is this somebody -- are you talking about something that's happened?
No. I'm just saying --
Making up an example, yeah.
-- what they all do. Example. They'll do it. Like a friend of mine come in and asked me to go play a
little old thing they had, a parade in the middle of the street out here, and they asked me to go play.
When was that?
Well, it's been a couple of months ago.
Oh, I see.
That's before you started coming here.
Yeah.
And I told them okay. So we played little gigs around here together.
Uh-huh.
So that night I didn't feel like it, but I was ready to go if he had come for me.
Uh-huh.
But the son of a bitch didn't come.
Uh-huh.
So, when he did come I told him no. You disappointed me once, why should I?
You mean he came back again for you?
Some other time.
Yeah, right.
And I told him no. I'm setting here ready for him to come, unnerved anyway, you know, because I knew I had to go out and do it, and this son of a bitch doesn't even come.
Yeah, I had that happen to me.
That's a hell of a feeling.
That happened to me once. In fact, you know, somebody I thought was a friend and --
Yeah.
-- you change your mind about it sometimes.
That's right. Wouldn't even let you know.

I had a whole thing. I had a whole set organized, we had rehearsed and everything. So I had this one set, and it was organized around him being a guest, you know, like guest star, I'd call him up from the audience.
Uh-huh.
But it was all rehearsed.
Uh-huh.
We did quite a lot of rehearsal, made arrangements and everything. A big deal, right.
It's cold, boy.

Half an hour before I was supposed to go over to play -- now, I put a lot of energy into that, you see. I played according to my own arrangements. He calls me up a half an hour before and said he's going for Washington, D. C. I'm in Philly, and he says, "Well, I've got this friend of mine, and blah, blah, blah, come down and play, and I said, "Well, are you getting paid for it?" and he says, "No, I'm getting paid tomorrow night and the next night, but tonight I want to come
down and learn the material." I said, "Man. Okay, we'll see you later. Later."
That's cold, boy.
I don't want to take food out of anybody's mouth, you know, if something comes up.
Give me a cigarette, honey.
Daddy, I don't have one. Unless you have some in your room.
Well, the only way you'll know is look.
I think Skip has some.
Well, Skip isn't here.
Oh.
So that's what I'm saying, boy. There ain't nothing. That's why I cut out of show business for awhile, you know, until I did get well.
Uh-huh.
To go out and take a whole lot more crap. I hope I don't have to do it.
Well, you don't feel that way about playing music. You're talking about a lot of the other stuff.
Attitudes of people.
Yeah.
You don't blame me.
I know what you're talking about.
Because it's common sense, Chuck. Now, you go out there in the street knowing what you're going to do
that night, and go in there and here comes two or three musicians that's been playing with you -- is it lit, honey?
(Unintelligible) No, that's -- the other end.
The other end. You've got it backwards. There you go.
And the best thing to do is don't go with them, so you won't get in no trouble like that. You understand what I mean, now?
Well, sure. People reveal themselves.
Yeah, sure. they rip you off.
They show where they're at.
They rip you off.
